thread_text:
alex: Hey folks, quick questionwe're planning a volunteer day on Fri and some folks will need to take partial day PTO. Do we treat that as normal PTO or can they use volunteer hours?

sam (People Ops): Good Q. We don't have a separate "volunteer hours" bank currently. For volunteer events during work hours, employees should use PTO or a floating holiday if they have one. Managers can approve unpaid time off in special cases but that's rare.

marta: What about people who worked extra hours earlier in the week and want to use comp for the afternoon?

sam (People Ops): Comp time still requires prior accrual and manager signoff in the HR portal. For one-off volunteer events we usually allow comp only if it's already accrued; otherwise PTO is expected. Manager must document approval in the portal notes.

alex: Okay thanks. I'll send a calendar invite and mark on the RSVP whether people will be taking PTO.

lee: Small note  if the event is company-sponsored and we reimburse travel/meal costs, please submit expenses under "Volunteering" category and tag People Ops.

payroll-bot: Reminder: Floating holidays expire at year-end unless carried per policy. Use code FLOAT for floating holiday entries. Link to policy: https://hr.redwood.example/pto/policy.pdf

alex: Got it. I'll include that link on the invite. Thanks everyone.
